subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What public web egress boundary should OpenClaw expose for this request: a scoped direct `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, a managed-proxy-owned policy, or a cross-tool fetch/search/browser policy?
rationale: The issue adds an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the current related PRs make different product/security tradeoffs that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch Allowlist First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while keeping deny, search, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make Managed Proxy the Boundary
options.body: Pause local `web_fetch` config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Design Cross-Tool Policy
options.body: Require a broader design covering fetch, search, browser, providers, plugins, redirects, and caches before any public egress config lands.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch Allowlist First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while keeping deny, search, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across the SSRF, guarded fetch, and web-fetch runtime surfaces involved in the boundary choice.
